chinese_source: Quilon (Tarisapalli) copper plates (NON-CHINESE external anchor; this field carries the dating record per schema)
date_raw: 5th regnal year of the Chera king Sthanu Ravi Kulasekhara
event: Ayyan Adikal, chief of Kollam, grants land and privileges to the Tarisapalli church under the Persian merchant Maruvan Sapir Iso; the witness plate carries signatures in Pahlavi, Kufic Arabic and Judeo-Persian
firmness_reason: Dated by the regnal year of an epigraphically anchored Chera king; the plates survive; the Pahlavi witness signatures were edited by Cereti (2009)
indian_entity: Tarisapalli church, Kollam (Quilon) — East Syriac-linked Christian community in Kerala
notes: Proves a chartered, Persian-linked Christian church on the Malabar coast by 849 — and nothing about its founder. Community tradition associates the migration behind the grant with Mar Sabor and Mar Proth (arrival c. 825), but the plates name Maruvan Sapir Iso; the identification is traditional, not epigraphic.
references: Cereti, 'The Pahlavi Signatures on the Quilon Copper Plates' (2009)
